options_ranked.title: Contract-Permitted Material Adjustment with Automatic Sunset
options_ranked.description: Deploy a separately stated, temporary material adjustment on Synthetic Blend Engine Oil and Conventional Engine Oil only for non-anchor customers whose contracts permit it. Use an agreed reference cost, cap and sunset to distinguish the adjustment from permanent repricing. Queue anchor-account amendments for actual lock expiry; do not use a surcharge or rebate change to circumvent locked terms. This is an immediate revenue pass-through intervention, not a reduction in COGS. Leave unrelated products and the within-threshold periods 2026-006 through 2026-008 outside the rollout; no healthy product segment is identified.
options_ranked.rationale: A contract-permitted adjustment can improve net realization before anchor-account renewals, while a sunset limits customer exposure if reference input costs reverse. Cost-to-serve and measurement-integrity disciplines require an actual cost basis, rather than treating parallel product declines as evidence of inflation. The intervention pulls net_revenue-to-gross_margin_pct; it offsets, but does not reduce, COGS.
options_ranked.time_to_value: First eligible invoices within 15–45 days; anchor-account contribution only after actual lock expiry.

arguments_for: A temporary adjustment offers near-term realization on flexible contracts while respecting the explicit anchor-account price lock.
arguments_against: Customers can offset the adjustment through rebates or reduced purchases, and no eligible customer revenue share is supplied.
key_questions: What cap and sunset will secure acceptance without offsetting concessions?

arguments_for: An explicit reference-cost formula links the adjustment to an auditable cost component; base oil is a client-confirmed component of COGS.
arguments_against: The confirmed accounting relationship does not establish that base oil prices increased, and a surcharge is not procurement savings.
key_questions: Do current accepted supplier terms support the proposed adjustment, and what reference-cost decline automatically removes it?

arguments_for: A reversible adjustment preserves participation choices while distinguishing recoverable price-cost lag from persistently weak account economics.
arguments_against: Temporary recovery can prolong service to unattractive accounts if renewal decisions ignore contribution after the adjustment expires.
key_questions: Which accounts will lose discretionary growth support if they remain below the approved contribution floor after adjustment?

implementation_triggers: Issue adjustments only after Legal confirms eligibility and the customer accepts required terms.
Activate the formula only where the existing procurement record supports its stated material-cost basis.
Apply the contractual sunset when the agreed reference cost crosses the removal threshold.
Activate anchor amendments only after lock expiry, without recognizing future-quarter recovery in current-period results.
prerequisites: Approved reference-cost formula, cap, customer notice and sunset clause.
Billing configuration that excludes all locked anchor accounts and prevents duplicate charges.
An agreed customer-retention and gross-profit stop rule.
Separate current-period eligible sales from future renewal benefits in the authorized business case.

impact_estimate.basis: The prescribed Stage 1 range targets 3.5–5.8 percentage points of Synthetic Blend Engine Oil's 7.14-point decline through permitted material adjustments and post-expiry amendments, although the originating proposal's component arithmetic does not support that range or its 90-day timing.

key_assumptions.assumption: Anchor-account list prices cannot be increased mid-quarter.
key_assumptions.provenance: The known manual constraint explicitly identifies a contractual mid-quarter price-lock clause on Lubricants anchor accounts.

key_assumptions.assumption: Some non-anchor contracts permit a temporary material adjustment.
key_assumptions.provenance: Legal sign-off on executed customer clauses and accepted amendments must identify eligible invoices before billing.

key_assumptions.assumption: A material-cost increase exists that can credibly support the adjustment.
key_assumptions.provenance: Comparable accepted supplier prices must exceed the agreed reference cost; stable or falling prices would falsify this justification.

key_assumptions.assumption: Customers will accept the adjustment without equivalent concessions or material lost contribution.
key_assumptions.provenance: Initial adjusted invoices, credit notes and retained orders must show a positive net gross-profit change.

flagged_side_effects: An adjustment can be perceived as an indirect price increase even when legally permitted.
Future-quarter amendments cannot recover current-period reported margin retroactively.
The prescribed recovery range is larger than the originating component calculations support.

options_ranked.title: Renewal-Gated Repricing and Margin-Protected Bundles
options_ranked.description: Prepare durable repricing for Synthetic Blend Engine Oil and Conventional Engine Oil, activating anchor-account changes only after contractual lock expiry. Pilot optional bundles solely in eligible non-anchor channels, with a positive incremental gross-profit floor after discounts and fulfillment costs. Synthetic Blend currently exceeds Conventional margin by only 1.48 points and is itself deteriorating; restore its realized unit economics before promoting a shift toward it. Do not intervene across unrelated products or the within-threshold periods 2026-006 through 2026-008. No healthy product benchmark or validated premium-additive margin is supplied.
options_ranked.rationale: Price-volume-mix decomposition supports separating realized repricing from any bundle contribution, while customer profitability analysis prevents nominal price gains being surrendered through concessions. The confirmed net_revenue-to-gross_margin_pct relationship supports the pricing mechanism, not the asserted premium mix benefit. Bundle expansion is therefore conditional on actual incremental economics rather than product positioning.
options_ranked.time_to_value: Eligible non-anchor bundles within 30–90 days; anchor-account repricing after actual lock expiry, potentially 90–180 days.

arguments_for: Renewal-cycle repricing directly addresses realized revenue on Synthetic Blend Engine Oil, whose margin fell from 27.78% to 20.64%.
arguments_against: At current margins, Synthetic Blend exceeds Conventional by only 1.48 points, so a large bundle-led mix benefit is not supported by the supplied product economics.
key_questions: Which renewals can accept the proposed price schedule without rebates or volume concessions offsetting the gain?

arguments_for: A fulfillment-cost floor prevents bundles from increasing distribution or packaging COGS, both identified as confirmed COGS components.
arguments_against: Pricing does not remove any underlying input-cost exposure, and the input does not establish whether base oil inflation caused the decline.
key_questions: Will the released bundle specification preserve incremental gross profit after packaging, freight and discount costs?

arguments_for: A limited bundle pilot preserves portfolio flexibility without assuming that declining engine-oil categories warrant immediate exit.
arguments_against: Renewal optimization retains the existing participation footprint even if demand or competitive economics have structurally weakened; the supplied data does not distinguish that possibility.
key_questions: What minimum retained gross profit will determine whether an account is renewed rather than de-emphasized?

implementation_triggers: Activate anchor-account price changes only when the contractual lock has expired.
Release a non-anchor bundle only after its approved offer shows positive incremental gross profit without changing protected contractual terms.
Stop bundle expansion if realized contribution falls below the approved standalone alternative.
prerequisites: Legal approval of renewal effective dates and eligible non-anchor offer terms.
Sales compensation and discount authority aligned to net realized margin rather than bundle volume.
Existing SKU economics must support each proposed additive package; no premium-margin prior is accepted as a substitute.
Treat the recovery anchor as a conditional scenario, not an underwritten forecast.

impact_estimate.basis: The prescribed Stage 1 range targets 3.2–5.1 percentage points of Synthetic Blend Engine Oil's 7.14-point decline through renewal repricing and margin-protected bundles, but remains conditional because eligible revenue coverage and bundle contribution are not established.

key_assumptions.assumption: Synthetic Blend currently has better margin than Conventional, but both require repair.
key_assumptions.provenance: Synthetic Blend is 20.64%, down 7.14 points; Conventional is 19.16%, down 6.61 points.

key_assumptions.assumption: A sufficiently large share of eligible sales will retain a 3–4% net price increase.
key_assumptions.provenance: Signed renewals and realized invoices must show the net increase after concessions, alongside retained customer volume.

key_assumptions.assumption: Optional bundles can add margin beyond the modest observed engine-oil margin spread.
key_assumptions.provenance: Pilot bundle invoices and fulfillment costs must show incremental gross profit exceeding the standalone purchase alternative.

key_assumptions.assumption: Most targeted anchor contracts become actionable within 90–180 days.
key_assumptions.provenance: Executed contract schedules must contain lock-expiry dates within that interval; the input supplies the clause but not expiry dates.

flagged_side_effects: A premium label does not guarantee a profitable bundle; discounting or added fulfillment cost could worsen Gross Margin %.
Customers may reduce purchases or demand offsetting rebates after renewal repricing.

options_ranked.title: Gate Specialty Reallocation on Restored Contribution
options_ranked.description: Reallocate discretionary sales effort and inventory from Conventional Engine Oil toward economically and technically suitable specialty demand, initially using Compressor Oil rather than an assumed High Mileage premium. Compressor Oil has a higher current margin, 28% versus Conventional's 19.16%, but has also fallen 5.86 points; first protect its delivered margin through approved order-size, freight and discount terms, then release incremental capacity only for orders meeting the contribution floor. High Mileage remains outside the initial shift because no margin observation is supplied. Preserve contracted engine-oil supply and leave the within-threshold periods 2026-006 through 2026-008 outside remediation. This is resource reallocation across distinct applications, not a claim that compressor products substitute for engine oil.
options_ranked.rationale: Portfolio participation analysis supports allocating incremental resources by actual delivered contribution rather than defending every conventional-grade sale. Compressor Oil's observed 28% margin supplies a better starting point than unverified specialty estimates, but its deterioration requires margin protection before expansion. The case does not assume lower base-oil intensity, verified High Mileage margins, or structural category decline; the supplied enterprise recovery anchor remains unsupported.
options_ranked.time_to_value: Contribution-protected orders within 60–90 days; material portfolio reallocation over 3–12 months.

arguments_for: Compressor Oil's observed 28% margin exceeds Conventional's 19.16%, giving targeted selling effort an evidence-based margin differential.
arguments_against: Different product applications mean conventional demand cannot simply be converted into specialty demand; the input supplies no specialty pipeline.
key_questions: Which contracted specialty orders can absorb reallocated capacity without displacing higher-contribution sales?

arguments_for: Freight, order-size and discount gates can protect delivered contribution before allocation expands, consistent with distribution and packaging being COGS components.
arguments_against: The input establishes neither spare specialty capacity nor lower base-oil intensity, and lower conventional throughput could worsen fixed-cost absorption.
key_questions: Can the production plan fulfill incremental specialty orders while preserving committed supply and acceptable absorption?

arguments_for: Resource reallocation addresses participation choices rather than relying exclusively on repricing deteriorating engine-oil products.
arguments_against: Compressor Oil is also down 5.86 points, so it is not an unaffected internal benchmark, and the original enterprise uplift arithmetic is overstated.
key_questions: What contribution and capacity-release thresholds must be met before conventional inventory or selling effort is withdrawn?

implementation_triggers: Release incremental specialty inventory only against technically suitable orders meeting an approved delivered-margin floor.
Begin reallocation only after Compressor Oil's offer terms protect its contribution at the planned selling price and cost.
Withdraw discretionary conventional support only after contractual supply commitments and absorption guardrails are satisfied.
Suspend expansion if incremental specialty contribution falls below the displaced conventional contribution.
prerequisites: An executable specialty order book and production slots, not assumed interchangeability with engine-oil demand.
Approved Compressor Oil freight, discount and minimum-order terms.
Preservation of anchor-account prices and contractual service obligations.
No investment authorization based on the stated enterprise recovery range until an executable allocation plan supports its magnitude.

impact_estimate.basis: The prescribed Stage 1 enterprise recovery range of 3.2–5.1 percentage points relies on reallocation toward higher observed margin, but the 8.84-point Compressor-versus-Conventional spread and the proposal's assumed 35% starting weight and 30–40% shift imply only about 0.93–1.24 points, while the broader reported decline is 4.49 points.

key_assumptions.assumption: Compressor Oil currently offers a higher reported margin than Conventional, despite its own deterioration.
key_assumptions.provenance: Compressor Oil reports 28% versus 33.86%; Conventional Engine Oil reports 19.16% versus 25.77%, giving an observed current spread of 8.84 points.

key_assumptions.assumption: Incremental specialty demand exists at margins comparable to the observed Compressor Oil average.
key_assumptions.provenance: Accepted incremental specialty orders must retain the approved delivered-margin floor after acquisition, freight and discount costs.

key_assumptions.assumption: Capacity and working capital can be redirected without material conversion cost or stranded overhead.
key_assumptions.provenance: The released production and inventory plan must preserve committed service and show no material adverse absorption or conversion charges.

key_assumptions.assumption: The proposal's 35% conventional weight and 30–40% reallocation are executable.
key_assumptions.provenance: The authorized revenue-weighted allocation schedule must match those shares; Stage 1 states them without supporting observations.

flagged_side_effects: Specialty positioning does not establish lower commodity exposure or superior incremental margins; High Mileage economics and lower base-oil intensity remain unsupported.
Compressor Oil is itself deteriorating, so expanding it before protecting contribution can move resources into another weakening segment.
Lower conventional throughput can strand overhead, weaken service and sacrifice gross-profit dollars even if the reported margin percentage rises.

solutions.recommendation_rationale: For the required first-move selection, authorize only the bounded, contract-permitted adjustment pilot: Synthetic Blend Engine Oil fell 7.14 points to 20.64%, and eligible non-anchor realization can act before protected anchor renewals. Its confirmed mechanism is net revenue improving Gross Margin %, not demonstrated base-oil inflation or cost reduction. The moderator flags the 3.5–5.8-point estimate, so this selection does not endorse that forecast or establish council consensus.

problem_reframe.situation: Gross Margin % declined year to date. The problem statement reports a 7.14 percentage-point decline to 20.64%, matching Synthetic Blend Engine Oil's movement from 27.78%. The broader deep-analysis highlight separately reports 29.94% versus 34.43%, a 4.49-point decline; these scopes must not be conflated.
problem_reframe.complication: Synthetic Blend Engine Oil, Conventional Engine Oil and Compressor Oil deteriorated, while periods 2026-006, 2026-007 and 2026-008 show positive deltas and are classified within threshold. No healthy product benchmark is supplied. Anchor-account list prices are locked mid-quarter, the proposed cost-inflation explanation remains unverified, and premium-product margin advantages cannot be assumed. The supplied recovery anchors also exceed what some proposal calculations support.
problem_reframe.question: Which independently executable intervention should defend Gross Margin % without breaching price locks, confusing segment recovery with enterprise recovery, or reallocating demand on unsupported premium-margin assumptions?

key_assumptions.assumption: The 20.64% current level and 7.14-point decline describe Synthetic Blend Engine Oil rather than a verified enterprise total.
key_assumptions.provenance: The Synthetic Blend Engine Oil change point reports 20.64% versus 27.78%, while what_is_highlights separately reports 29.94% versus 34.43%.

key_assumptions.assumption: A common input-cost shock contributes materially to the parallel engine-oil declines.
key_assumptions.provenance: Accepted supplier invoices and production consumption records would need to show higher comparable input cost, rather than discounting, allocation changes or product mix explaining the deterioration.

key_assumptions.assumption: The positive, within-threshold periods are not evidence of a transferable operating practice by themselves.
key_assumptions.provenance: The input identifies positive period deltas but supplies neither an internal_benchmark segment nor an associated operating practice.

proposed_option.title: Staged Mix-Driven Recovery via Selective Channel & Customer Repricing Post-Lock Expiry
proposed_option.description: Identify anchor accounts (largest by volume) whose price-lock clauses expire within 90–180 days and prepare tiered repricing schedules (+3–5% on Synthetic Blend, +2–3% on Conventional) to recover margin erosion. Simultaneously, execute targeted promotional bundling (Synthetic Blend + premium additive packages) on non-anchor channels to shift mix upward without violating contractual constraints on list prices.
proposed_option.mechanism: Direct mechanism: repricing post-lock expiry directly increases net revenue on locked-in volume, recovering gross margin % (confirmed causal link: net_revenue ↔ gross_margin_pct). Indirect mechanism: mix shift via bundling increases proportion of higher-margin SKUs in revenue composition, compounding recovery. Bypasses mid-quarter constraint by timing repricing to contractual renewal windows and using channel/product bundling (not list price) to drive mix on non-locked accounts.

impact_estimate.basis: Repricing on ~60–70% of Synthetic Blend volume (post-lock anchor accounts + non-locked channels) at +3–4% price realization, combined with 2–3 pp mix lift from bundling, recovers 3.2–5.1 pp of the 7.14 pp decline. Conservative estimate reflects execution risk and volume elasticity; high-end assumes 80%+ price stickiness and successful mix adoption.

proposed_option.title: Implement Immediate Base Oil Cost Pass-Through via SKU-Level Surcharge and Contract Amendment
proposed_option.description: Establish a temporary material cost adjustment (surcharge or tiered pricing) on Synthetic Blend and Conventional Engine Oil SKUs for non-anchor-account customers, and initiate formal contract renegotiation with anchor accounts to reset base price effective next quarter when price-lock expires. This directly addresses the base oil cost inflation trapped by the mid-quarter price-lock constraint and recovers margin without violating contractual obligations.
proposed_option.mechanism: Base oil cost inflation flows directly into COGS; the price-lock prevents list price increases on anchor accounts until next quarter. A surcharge on non-locked customers (if contractually permissible) or a volume-based rebate restructuring recovers margin immediately on flexible contracts. Anchor account renegotiation queues a permanent price adjustment to take effect when the lock expires, preventing margin erosion from repeating. This directly unblocks the COGS → Gross Margin % causal link.

impact_estimate.basis: Synthetic Blend margin fell 7.14pp due to base oil cost inflation. Conservative estimate recovers 3.5–5.8pp of the 7.14pp loss within 90 days, with full recovery by Q next via locked-in price increases.

proposed_option.title: Staged Mix Reallocation: Prioritize High Mileage and Specialty Formulations; De-Emphasize Conventional Grade Within Value Category
proposed_option.description: Rather than defend margin on commodity-grade conventional oils (where base oil cost inflation erodes all margin equally), reallocate sales effort and inventory allocation toward higher-margin specialty formulations (High Mileage, Compressor Oil) that command structural margin premiums and are less sensitive to base oil spot pricing. This reframes the portfolio from a commodity-price-taking position to a differentiated-product-led strategy, allowing margin recovery without triggering the price-lock clause (which applies to anchor accounts, not product mix shifts within the portfolio).
proposed_option.mechanism: Base oil cost inflation is compressing gross margin uniformly across conventional and synthetic-blend grades because both use the same base oil input. Reallocating volume from low-margin conventional (19.16% current) to higher-margin specialty products (e.g., High Mileage, Compressor Oil at estimated 25–28% margins) reduces the blended COGS exposure to commodity base oil while maintaining or growing total revenue. This is a portfolio reallocation play, not a pricing play, and thus avoids the contractual constraint. The mechanism works because specialty formulations carry higher value-add and lower base oil intensity per unit revenue.

impact_estimate.basis: If 30–40% of current Conventional Engine Oil volume (19.16% margin) is reallocated to specialty products averaging 26% margin, the blended margin on reallocated volume improves by ~6–7pp. Applied to a portfolio currently weighted ~35% toward conventional-grade oils, this yields a 2.1–2.5pp uplift to portfolio margin. Combined with modest volume hold on Synthetic Blend (currently 20.64%), a conservative recovery is 3.2–5.1pp toward the pre-crisis 27.78% level, representing a 15–25% recovery of the observed 7.14pp decline.
